observation_summary: The Joda-Time library incorrectly handles Daylight Saving Time (DST) transitions when using methods like .withHourOfDay(), .withMinuteOfHour(), etc. The resulting DateTime objects exhibit incorrect time zone offsets, failing to maintain the expected offset during the transition period.
hypothesis: The internal algorithm for calculating the new time during a DST transition fails to correctly account for the offset change when adjusting specific fields (hour, minute, etc.). It likely uses an incorrect procedure for determining the offset at the new time, causing it to revert to the wrong side of the DST cutover.
prediction: The fix will involve modifying the internal logic within the DateTime or Chronology classes that handles field adjustments during DST transitions, ensuring the offset is correctly recalculated or preserved based on the intended time.
experiment_rationale: The failure occurs consistently across multiple time-related adjustment methods (hour, minute, second, millis) during DST transitions, indicating a shared, flawed procedural logic for offset calculation rather than a simple missing check or wrong constant.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a procedural error in how the library calculates time adjustments during DST transitions. It is not a missing guard (Checking), a simple wrong value (Assignment), or a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object). It is a flaw in the computational strategy for handling time-zone-aware field updates, which fits the Algorithm/Method definition.
evidence_gaps: The actual production code implementation of the adjustment methods is not provided, only the test failures.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix might involve adding a check, the root cause is the incorrect procedural logic for calculating the new time, not just a missing validation.
The issue is about the internal consistency of a single object's state during an update, rather than a cross-cutting relationship between two distinct entities.
